nodes.title: Gke: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Gke. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Your GKE cluster needs to run a DaemonSet that collects logs from every node. Wh?
flashcards.back: A DaemonSet ensures that exactly one pod replica runs on every node (or a subset defined by node selectors). This is the standard pattern for log collectors, monitoring agents, and network plugins. Deployments and StatefulSets don't guarantee one-pod-per-node. CronJobs are for scheduled batch tasks.

flashcards.front: You need to deploy a containerized application that requires persistent disk sto?
flashcards.back: StatefulSets provide stable network identities (predictable pod names), ordered deployment/scaling, and per-pod persistent storage via volumeClaimTemplates. This is the correct choice for databases and stateful applications. Deployments support PVCs but don't provide stable pod identities.

flashcards.front: A GKE cluster's nodes are running out of memory. You want the cluster to automat?
flashcards.back: Cluster Autoscaler automatically adds or removes nodes based on pending pod scheduling requirements and resource utilization. HPA scales the number of pod replicas, not nodes. VPA adjusts resource requests for individual pods. Node auto-provisioning creates new node pools when needed, but Cluster Autoscaler is the primary node-scaling mechanism.

flashcards.front: Which command creates a new Kubernetes namespace called 'production' in your cur?
flashcards.back: kubectl create namespace production is the correct Kubernetes CLI command to create a namespace. GCP's gcloud tool doesn't have a direct namespace management command — namespaces are Kubernetes API objects managed via kubectl.

pairs.stem: Which command creates a new Kubernetes namespace called 'production' in your current GKE cluster context?
Your GKE cluster needs to run a DaemonSet that collects logs from every node. What is the correct Kubernetes resource to deploy?
A GKE cluster's nodes are running out of memory. You want the cluster to automatically add more nodes when resource utilization is high. What should you enable?
What is the function of a GKE Ingress resource?
pairs.option: Allocates an internal cluster IP for in-cluster service-to-service traffic

pairs.stem: A production GKE cluster must remain highly available if a single GCP zone fails. What cluster configuration achieves this?
pairs.option: Single-zone cluster with Pod Disruption Budgets enforced

pairs.stem: You need to deploy a containerized application that requires persistent disk storage and must maintain a stable network identity. Which GCP/Kubernetes resource is most appropriate?

nodes.title: IAM: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on IAM. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A developer needs to grant a service account the minimum permissions to read obj?
flashcards.back: roles/storage.objectViewer grants read access to objects within a bucket (storage.objects.get and storage.objects.list) without bucket-level administrative permissions, satisfying least privilege. roles/storage.objectAdmin permits write and delete on objects; roles/storage.bucketReader grants metadata read on the bucket itself; roles/storage.objectCreator allows uploads only.

flashcards.front: You are creating a VM instance that needs to access BigQuery and Cloud Storage w?
flashcards.back: Attaching a service account to a VM instance allows workloads to authenticate to Google Cloud APIs using the service account's identity via the metadata server — no key files needed. Storing key files on disk is a security risk. The default service account with Editor is overly permissive. Environment variables are not a secure long-term solution.

flashcards.front: Which IAM binding allows you to grant a role to all users of your Google Workspa?
flashcards.back: The domain: principal type grants access to all Google accounts in a Google Workspace (or Cloud Identity) domain. 'allUsers' grants access to everyone on the internet (unauthenticated included). 'allAuthenticatedUsers' covers all Google-signed-in users globally. group: requires a specific Google Group.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Google Cloud's Organization Policy Service?
flashcards.back: Organization Policy Service lets you set constraints on how GCP resources can be configured — for example, preventing public IP addresses on VMs, enforcing specific regions, or disabling service account key creation. These policies apply at the organization, folder, or project level and override individual IAM permissions.

pairs.stem: Which IAM binding allows you to grant a role to all users of your Google Workspace domain?
You need to give an external auditor read-only access to Cloud Logging audit logs in your project. Which predefined IAM role is most appropriate?
What is the purpose of Google Cloud's Organization Policy Service?
pairs.option: Manages billing accounts, budgets, and alerts for the organization

pairs.stem: You are creating a VM instance that needs to access BigQuery and Cloud Storage without storing credentials on disk. What is the recommended approach?
pairs.option: Attach a service account to the VM instance

pairs.stem: A developer needs to grant a service account the minimum permissions to read objects from a specific Cloud Storage bucket. Which IAM role should be granted at the bucket level?
You need to give a VM in Project A access to a Cloud Storage bucket in Project B. What is the correct approach?
pairs.option: Share the Project A owner credentials with the Project B service account

nodes.title: Networking: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Networking. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: You need to allow traffic from the internet to reach VMs on port 443 in your VPC?
flashcards.back: GCP VPCs use an implicit deny-all ingress rule by default. You must create an explicit ingress firewall rule allowing TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 (internet). External IPs alone don't open firewall ports. Cloud NAT is for outbound connectivity. VPC peering connects private networks.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a Cloud NAT gateway in GCP?
flashcards.back: Cloud NAT (Network Address Translation) allows VM instances without external IP addresses to make outbound connections to the internet while hiding their internal IPs. It does not allow unsolicited inbound connections. VPC peering is a separate service; Cloud VPN/Interconnect handles on-premises encryption.

flashcards.front: Which load balancer type should you choose to route HTTP/HTTPS traffic globally ?
flashcards.back: The Global External HTTP(S) Load Balancer is a Layer 7 proxy that uses Google's global network to route requests to the nearest healthy backend. It includes Cloud Armor for DDoS protection and supports URL-based routing. Internal load balancers are for private traffic. Regional load balancers don't offer global routing.

flashcards.front: You need to connect your on-premises network to a GCP VPC with dedicated bandwid?
flashcards.back: Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct physical connection between your on-premises network and Google's network, offering 10 Gbps or 100 Gbps links with 99.99% SLA when configured with redundancy. Cloud VPN uses the public internet with lower bandwidth. Partner Interconnect uses a service provider. Cloud NAT is for outbound internet access.

pairs.stem: What is the purpose of a Cloud NAT gateway in GCP?
pairs.option: Lets VMs without external IPs initiate outbound internet connections

pairs.stem: Which load balancer type should you choose to route HTTP/HTTPS traffic globally to backends in multiple regions with built-in DDoS protection?
You need to create a custom VPC network for a new project. When creating the VPC, you choose 'Custom' subnet mode. What does this mean?
pairs.option: The VPC uses IPv6 addressing by default on each subnet created in it

pairs.stem: You need to allow traffic from the internet to reach VMs on port 443 in your VPC. No current firewall rule exists. What must you do?
pairs.option: Create an ingress firewall rule allowing TCP:443 from 0.0.0.0/0

pairs.stem: Which GCP service provides Content Delivery Network (CDN) caching at Google's global edge locations for HTTP(S) load balanced backends?
You need to connect your on-premises network to a GCP VPC with dedicated bandwidth of 10 Gbps and low latency. SLAs are critical. Which connectivity option should you choose?
pairs.option: Cloud VPN over the public internet

nodes.title: Databases: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Databases. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: You need a fully managed relational database compatible with MySQL 8.0 on GCP. W?
flashcards.back: Cloud SQL is Google's fully managed relational database service supporting MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. Cloud Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column store. Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed relational database for massive scale. Firestore is a NoSQL document database.

flashcards.front: You need to store structured, schemaless JSON documents with real-time sync for ?
flashcards.back: Firestore (formerly Cloud Firestore/Datastore) is Google's serverless NoSQL document database with real-time sync, offline support, and automatic scaling — purpose-built for mobile and web applications. Cloud Bigtable is for time-series/analytics at massive scale. Cloud SQL/Spanner are relational databases.

flashcards.front: A Cloud SQL instance is experiencing high read latency under heavy load. You wan?
flashcards.back: Cloud SQL read replicas are asynchronous copies of the primary instance that serve read-only queries, offloading traffic without requiring application changes (just point read queries to the replica endpoint). Scaling up the instance tier helps but is more expensive. Memorystore helps but requires application-level cache logic. Spanner is a major migration.

flashcards.front: Which GCP service provides a globally distributed, strongly consistent relationa?
flashcards.back: Cloud Spanner is Google's proprietary globally distributed relational database providing ACID transactions, strong consistency, and horizontal scalability across regions — something no traditional relational database can do. Cloud SQL is regionally bound. Bigtable is NoSQL. AlloyDB is a high-performance PostgreSQL-compatible service but not globally distributed.

pairs.stem: You need a fully managed relational database compatible with MySQL 8.0 on GCP. Which service should you use?
Which GCP product provides a managed Redis or Memcached instance for application caching?
Which GCP service provides a globally distributed, strongly consistent relational database that automatically scales horizontally across regions?
A Cloud SQL instance is experiencing high read latency under heavy load. You want to offload read queries without changing the application architecture significantly. What should you add?
pairs.option: Upgrade the Cloud SQL tier to a larger machine

pairs.stem: You need to store structured, schemaless JSON documents with real-time sync for a mobile application. Which GCP database is the best fit?
You need to migrate a 5 TB PostgreSQL database from on-premises to Cloud SQL with minimal downtime. Which GCP service facilitates this?

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: You need to deploy a stateless web application that automatically scales from 0 ?
flashcards.back: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform that automatically scales containers from 0 to N based on incoming requests. It requires zero infrastructure management and is ideal for stateless workloads. App Engine Flexible and GKE require more configuration; Compute Engine MIGs need autoscaler setup.

flashcards.front: A VM instance has been accidentally deleted. You had taken a snapshot of its boo?
flashcards.back: To restore from a snapshot: (1) create a new persistent disk from the snapshot, (2) create a new VM instance using that disk as the boot disk. Snapshots are disk images, not full VM backups — they don't automatically recreate a VM. You'll need to reconfigure any VM-specific settings (network, labels, etc.).

flashcards.front: Which Compute Engine feature lets you run fault-tolerant batch workloads at up t?
flashcards.back: Spot VMs (the current name, replacing Preemptible VMs) offer up to 91% discount over on-demand pricing. They can be preempted with 30-second notice when Compute Engine needs capacity. They are ideal for batch processing, rendering, and fault-tolerant distributed workloads that can checkpoint progress.

flashcards.front: Which gcloud command connects you to a Compute Engine VM using OS Login without ?
flashcards.back: gcloud compute ssh INSTANCE_NAME handles SSH key management automatically when OS Login is enabled. It pushes your public key to the instance's metadata (or uses OS Login) and connects via IAP TCP tunneling if needed. Manual SSH with a key file requires managing keys yourself.

pairs.stem: Which Compute Engine feature lets you run fault-tolerant batch workloads at up to 91% discount, accepting that VMs may be preempted?
Your Cloud Storage bucket needs a policy that automatically deletes objects older than 30 days. What should you configure?
pairs.option: Retention policies on the bucket and object hold
